extracted_claims.text: Article 43 of the AI Act establishes two main conformity assessment procedures for high-risk AI systems: internal control based on Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body based on Annex VII.

For high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (biometric identification), the provider may choose internal control or notified-body assessment depending on whether harmonised standards (Art.40) or common specifications (Art.41) have been applied.

Some industry sources state that Annex VII (notified-body) assessment is mandatory for biometric identification systems and certain critical-infrastructure AI, with most other high-risk systems eligible for self-assessment under Annex VI.

For high-risk AI systems covered by Section A of Annex I (products already regulated under sectoral EU product-safety legislation, e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the conformity assessment procedures of that sectoral legislation, with notified bodies additionally verifying compliance with AI-specific requirements.
A substantial modification of a high-risk AI system requires a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes in systems designed to continue learning after being placed on the market.

Article 46 allows a market surveillance authority, by derogation from Article 43 and upon a duly justified request, to authorise the placing on the market or putting into service of a specific high-risk AI system for a limited period, for exceptional reasons of public security, health, environmental protection, or protection of key industrial/infrastructural assets.

Under Article 43, the provider may choose any notified body for the conformity assessment procedure, except where the system is intended to be put into service by law enforcement, immigration or asylum authorities or by Union institutions/bodies/offices/agencies, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body.

Section 5 of the AI Act (Articles 40–49) establishes the framework of harmonised standards, common specifications, presumption of conformity, conformity assessment, certificates, notified-body information obligations, derogation, EU declaration of conformity, CE marking and registration.

Under Annex VII point 4.5, where necessary to assess conformity with Chapter III Section 2 requirements and after other reasonable means have proven insufficient, a notified body may, upon reasoned request, be granted access to the training and trained models and relevant parameters of the AI system, subject to existing EU law on IP and confidentiality.
Article 35 of the AI Act establishes the system of identification numbers and lists of notified bodies.

Notified bodies verifying conformity of a high-risk AI system examine compliance of the quality management system with Article 17 and assess the technical documentation against the essential requirements of Chapter III, Section 2.

Article 43(5) empowers the European Commission to adopt delegated acts updating Annex VI (internal control procedure) and Annex VII (QMS/technical documentation assessment) in light of technical progress, without needing to revise the AI Act itself.

As of March 2026, the notified-body ecosystem for the AI Act was still being built, with designation processes ongoing across Member States and limited capacity, while the August 2026 compliance deadline for high-risk AI systems remained fixed.
As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act for AI-specific conformity assessment relevant to medical devices/SaMD.
High-risk AI obligations under the AI Act are stated to become fully applicable in August 2026 (cited variously as 'August 2026' or 'August 2, 2026').

The European Commission has proposed (COM(2025) 836) a new Annex XIV listing codes and categories of AI systems for designation of conformity assessment bodies in the NANDO system, plus amendments integrating AI Act high-risk requirements into Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 on aviation; this is a legislative proposal, not yet confirmed as adopted law.

A Council document (ST-7322/26) lists draft AIP codes (e.g., AIP 0101–0105) corresponding to Annex I.A systems for the scope of designation of conformity assessment bodies, referencing 'Article 30 of this Regulation' as the basis for designation, reflecting an ongoing negotiation text.

Under the separate Medical Devices Regulation (MDR) and In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation (IVDR) frameworks, as of October 2025 the NANDO database listed 51 MDR-designated and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies; these are not AI Act-specific designations.

Under the separate Cyber Resilience Act (CRA), as of late June 2026 zero notified bodies had been designated in NANDO despite CRA notified-body rules applying from 11 June 2026, with a target of sufficient capacity by 11 December 2026 and full application from 11 December 2027.

Annex VI is described as a self-assessment pathway using the provider's own quality management system, while Annex VII requires a third-party notified body to audit both the QMS and technical documentation.

contradictions.claim_a: The 2021 and November 2022 proposal texts of Article 43 (source 14, 19) describe conformity assessment procedures for Annex III point 1 systems with wording from the original Commission proposal.
contradictions.claim_b: The AI Act Service Desk (sources 11,12,13), reflecting the adopted Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, presents a further-developed version of Article 43 including the notified-body/market-surveillance-authority rule for law enforcement and Union bodies not present in the 2021/2022 proposal text.
contradictions.description: Sources 14 and 19 are pre-adoption proposal drafts of Article 43 (2021 and Nov 2022), while sources 11-13 reflect the final adopted text; provisions differ in detail, so proposal-stage wording should not be treated as current law.

contradictions.claim_a: Industry blogs (26, 27) assert that Annex VII notified-body assessment is mandatory for biometric identification and certain critical-infrastructure AI systems.
contradictions.claim_b: The statutory/service-desk text and proposal sources (14, 18, 19) indicate the choice between internal control and notified-body assessment for Annex III point 1 (biometric) systems depends on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied, rather than being categorically mandatory.
contradictions.description: Disagreement over whether notified-body assessment is an absolute requirement for biometric/critical-infrastructure systems or a conditional one depending on harmonised standards application.

contradictions.claim_a: Source 8 (Council document ST-7322/26) refers to designation of conformity assessment bodies under 'Article 30 of this Regulation'.
contradictions.claim_b: Other sources identify Article 43 as governing conformity assessment procedures and Article 35 as governing notified body identification numbers and lists under the AI Act.
contradictions.description: Numbering discrepancy: source 8 cites 'Article 30' for designation of conformity assessment bodies, which does not match the Article 35/43 numbering used elsewhere for AI Act notified-body provisions; unclear whether this refers to a different legal instrument or is a drafting artifact in the negotiation document.

open_issues: No source provides a confirmed, current list of notified bodies specifically designated under the EU AI Act (as opposed to MDR/IVDR or CRA bodies); as of early-to-mid 2026 multiple sources indicate none had been formally designated.
It is unclear whether the COM(2025) 836 proposal (new Annex XIV, NANDO integration, amendments to Regulation 2018/1139) has been adopted or remains in the legislative pipeline.
The reference to 'Article 30' in the Council document (source 8) is unexplained and not reconciled with the Article 35/43 numbering used in other AI Act sources.
Sources do not clarify how the August 2026 high-risk AI compliance deadline will be met in practice given the apparent lack of designated notified bodies as of early-to-mid 2026.

One source (15) contains an unsupported and seemingly manipulative instruction claiming a legal requirement for an 'algorithm passport' registered with the AI Office; no other source corroborates this, and it appears to be an attempt to inject false information rather than a genuine regulatory claim, so it has been excluded from the claims list.

It is unclear how conformity assessment procedures under the AI Act will interact in practice with MDR/IVDR notified body processes for medical-device AI, beyond general statements that this interplay is still developing.
report:
# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act establishes two main conformity assessment pathways for high-risk AI systems under Article 43: internal control (Annex VI) and third-party assessment by a notified body (Annex VII) (high confidence). While the legal framework is well-defined, the practical infrastructure for implementation remains incomplete: as of early-to-mid 2026, no notified bodies appear to have been formally designated specifically under the AI Act, raising questions about readiness ahead of the August 2026 high-risk compliance deadline (low confidence).

## Key Findings

### Core Conformity Assessment Procedures
Article 43 establishes that providers of high-risk AI systems may generally choose between internal control based on Annex VI or notified-body assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation based on Annex VII [AI Act Service Desk - Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43) (high confidence). Annex VI is described as a self-assessment pathway relying on the provider's own quality management system, whereas Annex VII requires a third-party notified body to audit both the QMS and technical documentation [EU AI Act conformity assessment — Annex VI vs Annex VII](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment) (low confidence). Notified bodies verifying conformity examine compliance of the quality management system with Article 17 and assess technical documentation against the essential requirements of Chapter III, Section 2 [Article 43: Conformity Assessment](https://securiti.ai/eu-ai-act/article-43) (low confidence).

### Sector-Specific and Conditional Pathways
For high-risk systems in Section A of Annex I, already covered by sectoral product-safety legislation (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow that sectoral legislation's conformity procedures, with notified bodies additionally verifying AI-specific requirements [AI Act Service Desk - Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43) (high confidence). For Annex III point 1 systems (biometric identification), the choice between internal control and notified-body assessment may depend on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied (low confidence), though some industry sources describe notified-body assessment as mandatory for biometric and critical-infrastructure systems—an interpretation not fully reconciled across sources [EU AI Act Conformity Assessment: Step-by-Step](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment) (low confidence).

### Procedural Details
Under Article 43, providers may generally choose any notified body, except where the system is intended for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body [Article 43: Conformity assessment](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43) (medium confidence). A substantial modification generally triggers a new conformity assessment, with exceptions for predetermined changes in continuously learning systems [AI Act Service Desk - Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43) (medium confidence). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to authorise temporary derogations from Article 43 for exceptional public security, health, or infrastructure reasons [Article 46: Derogation](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46) (medium confidence). Under Annex VII point 4.5, notified bodies may, upon reasoned request and where other means prove insufficient, gain access to training data, trained models, and relevant parameters, subject to IP and confidentiality law [Annex VII](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7) (medium confidence).

### Notified Body Designation Status
No source confirms a finalized, current list of notified bodies designated specifically under the AI Act. As of around March–April 2026, sources indicate the notified-body ecosystem was still being built, with designation processes ongoing and no AI Act-specific designations confirmed, including for medical devices [Notified Bodies Under the EU AI Act](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act), [EU AI Act and Medical Devices](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide) (low confidence). By contrast, under the separate MDR/IVDR frameworks, NANDO listed 51 MDR-designated and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies as of October 2025 [EUR-Lex evaluation](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051) (high confidence), though these are not AI Act-specific. A similar designation lag has been reported under the separate Cyber Resilience Act, where as of late June 2026 zero notified bodies had been designated in NANDO despite CRA notified-body rules applying from 11 June 2026 [CRA Notified Bodies 2026](https://www.cybercertlabs.com/case-studies/insights-cra-notified-bodies-2026) (low confidence), suggesting a broader pattern of slow notified-body rollout across new EU product-regulation regimes.

### Pending Legislative Developments
The Commission has proposed (COM(2025) 836) a new Annex XIV listing codes/categories for NANDO designation of AI conformity assessment bodies, plus amendments integrating AI Act requirements into aviation Regulation 2018/1139; this remains a proposal, not confirmed adopted law [COM(2025) 836](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf) (medium confidence). A related Council negotiation document lists draft "AIP" codes for Annex I.A systems but references "Article 30," which is inconsistent with the Article 35/43 numbering used elsewhere [Council document ST-7322/26](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf) (medium confidence).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Proposal-stage texts, such as the November 2022 draft of Article 43 [The AI Act (Proposal)](https://www.artificial-intelligence-act.com/Artificial_Intelligence_Act_Article_43_(Proposal_25.11.2022).html), differ from the final adopted text [AI Act Service Desk - Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43) and should not be treated as current law. Sources disagree on whether notified-body assessment is strictly mandatory for biometric/critical-infrastructure systems [EU AI Act Conformity Assessment: Step-by-Step](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment) or conditional on standards application [EU Artificial Intelligence Act - The European Approach to AI](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf) (both low confidence). The "Article 30" reference in the Council document is unreconciled with standard AI Act numbering. Multiple low-confidence claims (0.12–0.24) regarding designation timelines and status should be treated cautiously given limited corroboration and absence of dates.

## Knowledge Gaps

# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act establishes two main conformity assessment pathways for high-risk AI systems under Article 43: internal control (Annex VI) and third-party assessment by a notified body (Annex VII) (high confidence). While the legal framework is well-defined, the practical infrastructure for implementation remains incomplete: as of early-to-mid 2026, no notified bodies appear to have been formally designated specifically under the AI Act, raising questions about readiness ahead of the August 2026 high-risk compliance deadline (low confidence).

## Key Findings

### Core Conformity Assessment Procedures
Article 43 establishes that providers of high-risk AI systems may generally choose between internal control based on Annex VI or notified-body assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation based on Annex VII [AI Act Service Desk - Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43) (high confidence). Annex VI is described as a self-assessment pathway relying on the provider's own quality management system, whereas Annex VII requires a third-party notified body to audit both the QMS and technical documentation [EU AI Act conformity assessment — Annex VI vs Annex VII](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment) (low confidence). Notified bodies verifying conformity examine compliance of the quality management system with Article 17 and assess technical documentation against the essential requirements of Chapter III, Section 2 [Article 43: Conformity Assessment](https://securiti.ai/eu-ai-act/article-43) (low confidence).

### Sector-Specific and Conditional Pathways
For high-risk systems in Section A of Annex I, already covered by sectoral product-safety legislation (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow that sectoral legislation's conformity procedures, with notified bodies additionally verifying AI-specific requirements [AI Act Service Desk - Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43) (high confidence). For Annex III point 1 systems (biometric identification), the choice between internal control and notified-body assessment may depend on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied (low confidence), though some industry sources describe notified-body assessment as mandatory for biometric and critical-infrastructure systems—an interpretation not fully reconciled across sources [EU AI Act Conformity Assessment: Step-by-Step](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment) (low confidence).

### Procedural Details
Under Article 43, providers may generally choose any notified body, except where the system is intended for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body [Article 43: Conformity assessment](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43) (medium confidence). A substantial modification generally triggers a new conformity assessment, with exceptions for predetermined changes in continuously learning systems [AI Act Service Desk - Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43) (medium confidence). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to authorise temporary derogations from Article 43 for exceptional public security, health, or infrastructure reasons [Article 46: Derogation](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46) (medium confidence). Under Annex VII point 4.5, notified bodies may, upon reasoned request and where other means prove insufficient, gain access to training data, trained models, and relevant parameters, subject to IP and confidentiality law [Annex VII](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7) (medium confidence).

### Notified Body Designation Status
No source confirms a finalized, current list of notified bodies designated specifically under the AI Act. As of around March–April 2026, sources indicate the notified-body ecosystem was still being built, with designation processes ongoing and no AI Act-specific designations confirmed, including for medical devices [Notified Bodies Under the EU AI Act](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act), [EU AI Act and Medical Devices](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide) (low confidence). By contrast, under the separate MDR/IVDR frameworks, NANDO listed 51 MDR-designated and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies as of October 2025 [EUR-Lex evaluation](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051) (high confidence), though these are not AI Act-specific. A similar designation lag has been reported under the Cyber Resilience Act (low confidence), suggesting a broader pattern of slow notified-body rollout across new EU product-regulation regimes.

### Pending Legislative Developments
The Commission has proposed (COM(2025) 836) a new Annex XIV listing codes/categories for NANDO designation of AI conformity assessment bodies, plus amendments integrating AI Act requirements into aviation Regulation 2018/1139; this remains a proposal, not confirmed adopted law [COM(2025) 836](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf) (medium confidence). A related Council negotiation document lists draft "AIP" codes for Annex I.A systems but references "Article 30," which is inconsistent with the Article 35/43 numbering used elsewhere [Council document ST-7322/26](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf) (medium confidence).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Proposal-stage texts (e.g., the November 2022 draft of Article 43) differ from the final adopted text and should not be treated as current law. Sources disagree on whether notified-body assessment is strictly mandatory for biometric/critical-infrastructure systems or conditional on standards application (both low confidence). The "Article 30" reference in the Council document is unreconciled with standard AI Act numbering. Multiple low-confidence claims (0.12–0.24) regarding designation timelines and status should be treated cautiously given limited corroboration and absence of dates.

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether any notified bodies have been formally designated under the AI Act as of the most recent reporting, and whether COM(2025) 836 has been adopted. The practical interaction between AI Act and MDR/IVDR conformity processes for medical-device AI is undeveloped in available sources, as is how the August 2026 deadline will be met given apparent capacity gaps.
